options: A query that returns zero rows unexpectedly
Re-running the same query twice within one transaction and getting a different set of rows, because another transaction inserted or deleted matching rows in between
Reading another transaction's uncommitted change before it rolls back
Reading the same row twice and getting a different value each time
questions.explain: A phantom read is about the row SET changing -- new rows appearing or existing ones disappearing -- not an existing row's value changing.

questions.q: How is a phantom read different from a nonrepeatable read?
options: A nonrepeatable read is an existing row's value changing; a phantom read is entirely new or removed rows changing the result set
They are identical anomalies with different names
A nonrepeatable read involves INSERT/DELETE, a phantom read involves UPDATE
A phantom read can only happen under SERIALIZABLE
questions.explain: Nonrepeatable reads concern a value changing on an already-read row; phantom reads concern the overall set of qualifying rows changing via INSERT or DELETE.

questions.q: Why doesn't REPEATABLE READ prevent phantom reads?
options: REPEATABLE READ only locks rows it has already read -- it can't lock a row that didn't exist yet when the first query ran
REPEATABLE READ doesn't support SELECT COUNT(*) queries
REPEATABLE READ is actually looser than READ COMMITTED
REPEATABLE READ only applies to UPDATE statements, not SELECT
questions.explain: REPEATABLE READ holds locks on rows it has seen, but a newly inserted row was never seen, so there's nothing for it to lock -- it slips through the gap.

questions.q: What mechanism does SERIALIZABLE use that the other levels don't, to prevent phantoms?
options: Deadlock detection running more frequently
Range locks, which lock the 'gap' a query's predicate covers, not just rows that currently exist
Table-level exclusive locks on every table referenced
Row versioning, keeping a historical copy of every row
questions.explain: A range lock locks the entire range a predicate like 'BETWEEN 500 AND 1000' represents, so no new row can be inserted into that range until the transaction finishes.

questions.q: Across all four ANSI isolation levels, which allow phantom reads?
options: Only READ UNCOMMITTED allows it
READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, and REPEATABLE READ all allow it; only SERIALIZABLE prevents it
All four ANSI levels allow phantom reads
None of the four ANSI levels allow phantom reads
questions.explain: Phantom reads are the one anomaly that REPEATABLE READ still permits -- SERIALIZABLE is the only standard level strict enough to prevent it.
